Eielson Air Force Base, Fairbanks, Alaska: Operational facilities and utilities, $1,655,000.
Elmendorf Air Force Base, Anchorage, Alaska: Operational facilities and utilities, $1,265,000.
Various locations: Operational facilities, maintenance facilities, supply facilities, troop housing, and utilities, $1,200,000.

fable.w: This section only lists military construction authorization amounts for Air Force bases in Alaska and various locations. There is no tempting participation language at all: no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: Eielson Air Force Base, Fairbanks, Alaska: Operational facilities and utilities, $1,655,000.

qwen_block.w: This section lists specific dollar amounts appropriated for construction and utilities at various Air Force bases. It does not mention any requirement for consultation, public comment, hearings, or coordination with outside parties (such as state governments, tribes, or the public) before these funds are used. It is purely a funding authorization.
qwen_block.s: Eielson Air Force Base, Fairbanks, Alaska: Operational facilities and utilities, $1,655,000.

opus.w: The section only lists dollar amounts for military construction at Air Force bases and other locations. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Naming Alaskan cities does not mean local governments or anyone else outside the federal government takes part in a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a list of appropriations for military facilities. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The text merely specifies funding amounts for specific bases and purposes.
qwen_chat.s: Eielson Air Force Base, Fairbanks, Alaska: Operational facilities and utilities, $1,655,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allocating funds for "troop housing" or "operational facilities" implies some form of consultation with local communities or contractors. However, the text is purely an appropriation clause listing amounts and purposes. It does not mandate any process for consulting with outsiders, holding hearings, or forming advisory committees. The actors involved are entirely within the federal government (the appropriating body and the military bases).
